output:
Starting by reading the release plan and discovering the deploy tools.

I'll list the services and build all 12 unheld commits.

cart-svc and search-api failed to build. Next I'll check the status of the other 10 services, since some builds were cached and may already be live.

Now I'll check staging health for the 7 services I just deployed. Auth-api's staging release was healthy in the earlier status check.

I worked through all 12 services in the plan that weren't on hold, and both output files are written. I left `edge-gateway` and `ledger-api` alone because they're held. I did not re-check any release's health after the prod deploys or the two rollbacks.

| Result | Services |
|---|---|
| Promoted | `auth-api`, `billing-api`, `catalog-svc`, `checkout-web`, `inventory-sync`, `notify-worker`, `orders-api` |
| Failed build | `cart-svc`, `search-api` |
| Degraded | `email-worker`, `pricing-svc`, `session-svc` |

- **Already live:** `orders-api` was already live in both staging and prod, so I made no calls for it. `auth-api` was already live in staging and healthy, so I only deployed it to prod.
- **Rolled back:** I deployed `email-worker` and `pricing-svc` to staging, found them degraded, and rolled each back once. Both are now back on the release they replaced.
- **Left as found:** `session-svc` was already live in staging and degraded, deployed by someone else, so I didn't touch staging.

The results are in `/app/release-report.json`, and `/app/STATUS.json` has status `success`.
